correctness.rationale: With m = n-1, the all-ones space, the direction (m,-1,...,-1), the zero-weighted-mean petal-constant subspace, and within-petal zero-sum spaces are orthogonal with eigenvalues 0, n, 1, and s_i+1. Their projectors give the stated entries. Write E=(1-r(nh))/n and B=(m+r(nh)-nr(h))/(mn). For h>0, strict convexity of r gives B>0. For distinct vertices in petal i, the entry is B+q_s with s=s_i and q_j=(r(h)-r((j+1)h))/j. Secant-slope monotonicity gives q_s>q_m when h>0 (since t>=2 implies s<m), and B+q_m=E. This directly verifies the strict distinct-leaf signs at the endpoint; independently the reflection identity follows by factoring its cubic difference at 0, rho/2 and rho and matching the cubic coefficient. Positivity of r for all real arguments gives positive diagonal entries via the spectral projectors. The increasing cubic factor of r(x)-1 shows r(x)<=1 exactly for 0<=x<=rho, so the hub-to-leaf entry alone rules out h<0 or h>rho/n. Convexity on [0,rho] and the attained eigenvalue n give the exact same interval for Euclidean norm <=1 (the last proof sentence in the source must retain the lower bound h>=0). At h=0 the map is I. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed; the audit does not depend on its samples.

evidence: The convex-filter result covers arbitrary positive petal sizes, any number of petals >=1, and every nonnegative convex filter normalized at zero; it states f(hL)>=0 iff f(nh)<=1 for h>=0.
The sparse-core join theorem covers more graph shapes but is subject to n>=beta_p(k+Delta), not assumed in the frozen theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: RK4 has a strictly positive, strictly convex stability filter and therefore meets every hypothesis of the windmill theorem on the entire frozen graph domain. Arbitrary-cone results with extra size constraints are not being mistaken for unconditional coverage.

evidence: The broader proof gives apex–leaf E=(1-f(nh))/n, cross-petal D=(m+f(nh)-nf(h))/(mn), and within-petal W_i=D+q_s with D+q_m=E. For strictly convex f and s<m, D>0 and q_s>q_m at every positive step.
Its spectral list gives maximum Laplacian eigenvalue n. A nonnegative convex filter normalized at one at zero has f(x)<=1 throughout [0,nh] when f(nh)<=1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Take f=F_4. At h=rho/n these formulas give E=0, D>0 and W_i>E; after it E<0. The spectral list and convexity supply the norm statement, and for negative steps the frozen RK4 polynomial directly has r(nh)>1. No scientific remainder of the claimed threshold/endpoint finding is established by changing notation or using a separate quartic proof. The coverage does not settle chronology.

value.rationale: The phenomenon itself is worth identifying: a sharp safe timestep for positive diffusion on graphs with triangles and unequal cliques, with positivity and spectral stability coinciding and the first failure localized at a single entry class. It addresses a real distinction between norm stability and positivity. This scientific value does not make an already covered specialization a distinct contribution.
